$description: Peace Intel design tokens. DTCG-shaped. Every token carries a rationale and, where one exists, a machine-checkable constraint. The constraints are the point: an engineer who hits an accessibility problem can fix the value at the source instead of forking the palette in a page scope, which is what produced the two-brand split documented in audit/DRIFT.md.

$meta.rule: Token names match what production already spells. Adoption is a values swap, not a rename.
$meta.currentPreference: 2026-09-24 — Nanum Myeongjo / DIN 2014 / Space Mono (decided). Raised surface DECIDED: hairline and wash used freely, warm rationed to the extreme case. Corners still open, defaulting to none, and that choice also decides whether registration exists at all. Rev 2 is frozen at handoff/archive/rev2-2026-09-24/. Pl. 12 gradient fields, Pl. 13 grid behaviour and Pl. 14 video treatment are EXPLORATIONS, held in handoff/explorations.css and deliberately outside the component catalog until one is chosen.

bg.$description: Page and card background. Warm off-white, never pure white.

$extensions.pi.rationale: The warm cast is the whole basis of the brand's depth. Chosen over a cooler blue variant in an A/B on 2026-07-08.
Locked decision 2026-07-11. A neutral-grey and an orange-wash alternative were both reviewed and rejected.
$extensions.pi.constraint: Do not substitute a neutral grey.

ink.$description: Primary text. Warm near-black. Also the fill for inverted elements.

$extensions.pi.rationale: Opaque, not alpha. The prototype's alpha inks composited below AA; production flattened them for the same reason. Opaque values can be tuned against a target; alpha values drift with whatever surface they land on.

The AA floor for body text. Solved against --panel, not --bg: an earlier revision measured 4.52:1 on the page but only 4.04:1 on a raised surface, so every piece of muted text on a card or a chat bubble was silently failing.

ink-35.$description: Faint text: timestamps, section markers, disabled states. Also hover border colour.

$extensions.pi.rationale: 3:1 is the WCAG floor for UI components and large text. Anything fainter cannot carry meaning.
Borders stay alpha deliberately. They sit on --bg and --panel alike and must composite against both. Production flattened this to #e2e0da, which is correct on --bg and slightly wrong on --panel.

line-2.$description: Stronger border: interactive chips, inputs, cards.

$extensions.pi.rationale: Separate from the text ramp so the opaque inks can be tuned for contrast without breaking hover states.

accent.$description: The one brand accent. Graphics, large type, fills, focus rings.

$extensions.pi.rationale: Used for meaning only: evidence, primary action, focus, active state. More than three or four accented spots in a view means it is over-accented.
$extensions.pi.warning: 4.18:1 FAILS AA for text under 24px. Use accent-text for small type. Production forked the palette to a brown (#8a5a2b) rather than splitting the token; that brown was REVIEWED AND REJECTED on 2026-09-24. Splitting the token solves the same problem without changing hue.
$extensions.pi.openQuestion: The original brief specified an EPI green accent. The prototype supersedes it with warm orange. Flagged for the board, not silently resolved.
$extensions.pi.decided: 2026-09-24 — warm orange is the accent. No second accent is carried.

accent-text.$description: Accent for any text under 24px. AA guaranteed.

$extensions.pi.rationale: A barely perceptible darkening of the brand orange that clears AA on BOTH the page and any raised surface. This is what makes the brand value usable for body text without adopting a different hue.

$extensions.pi.constraint: Must derive from accent. Production hardcodes rgba(217,72,28,.14), which disagrees with its own brown accent.
Highest-emphasis moments only. At most one element per view. Never on text, never on a large surface.
$extensions.pi.note: Not derived from accent. This is why the brown fork was hard to spot: CTAs stayed orange on the brown routes.

dark.$description: Full dark theme, applied by data-theme="dark". Ratios against dark.bg.

$extensions.pi.rationale: Warm near-black, not grey or blue-black.

$extensions.pi.note: Production ships #C2BFB9 (10.10:1), deliberately softer. Both pass; a taste call for Matt.

$extensions.pi.constraint: Never use the light-mode #D9481C on a dark background; it measures 4.05:1 there.

onDark.$description: A dark band or card INSIDE a light page (.on-dark), and the light-on-dark direction too (.surface--invert flips against the theme). Neither codebase had this layer; both hardcoded white-alpha, which meant dark bands inverted into light bands the moment a dark theme was applied. The ramp is solved against #211D16, the LIGHTER of the two band surfaces, so one ramp serves both a band on a light page and a band on a dark page.

$extensions.pi.rationale: Replaces a hardcoded #1C1A16 that was a fourth near-black with no token, distinct from --ink.
The light-mode accent measures only 4.05:1 on this surface, so the band needs the warmer end of the gradient.

serif.$description: Editorial voice: headlines, card titles, entry titles.

$extensions.pi.constraint: DIN 2014 has no Medium (500) cut. 500 rounds down to Regular. Step to 600 for visible emphasis, do not fake a 500.
$extensions.pi.note: Production dropped DIN 2014 when fonts.cdnfonts.com began 500ing on every load. That was the right call at the time. Self-hosted WOFFs now exist at Fonts/DIN2014/, so the stack can be reinstated.

mono.$description: Instrument labels: kickers, timestamps, citation chips, badges.

$extensions.pi.decided: 2026-09-24 — Nanum Myeongjo / DIN 2014 / Space Mono. The Source Serif 4 / DM Sans / JetBrains Mono alternative was reviewed and dropped. DM Sans remains the sans fallback.

typeScale.$description: Ten steps. Replaces 32 ad-hoc sizes found in problems.html and 25 in rotary-a.html.

$extensions.pi.constraint: A font-size that is not a step here is a bug. Add a step before using a new value.

eyebrow.$description: Four ladder steps for mono uppercase labels. Replaces thirteen letter-spacing values plus three in raw pixels. Tracking scales inversely with size.

$extensions.pi.constraint: Do not invent new size/tracking pairings. Use a step.

space.$description: 4px grid. The prototype had no spacing scale at all (DESIGN-TOKENS.md §8 says so) and grew to 24 distinct margin values in one page.

$extensions.pi.constraint: Every margin, padding and gap is a step here. Nothing off-grid.

radius.$description: Six steps, radius growing with surface size. OPEN QUESTION as of 2026-09-24: variety in radius is one of the most recognisable tells of a generated interface, so two flatter alternatives are under review behind data-radius. Nothing in components.css hardcodes a radius, so the switch reaches every element.

$extensions.pi.use: avatars, status dots, radio marks. Goes to 0 under data-radius=none, because a partial commitment to squareness is just decoration.

pi.options.soft: 4 / 6 / 8 / 12 / 14 / 20 — the default. Radius carries some of the hierarchy. Costs a decision per component.
pi.options.tight: 2 and 4 only. Corners become a manufacturing tolerance rather than a design decision; hierarchy moves onto the rules, the type and the surfaces. Circles stay circles.
pi.options.none: 0 everywhere, circles included. Every edge is a drawn line. A real test of whether the grid, hairlines and typography carry the character alone.

elevation.$description: Warm-tinted via --sh, always a tight contact shadow plus a soft distant one.

$extensions.pi.constraint: Elevation signals interactivity. Static content gets borders, not shadows.
Animate only box-shadow, border-color, background, transform, width and opacity. No bounces, no springs, nothing over .3s in-app. Always ship the reduced-motion kill switch.
$extensions.pi.language: 'Resolve, don't type.' No typewriter, terminal cursor, redaction bars or scanlines; those are costume. The primitives borrow from what intelligence work actually feels like: evidence resolving out of noise (.mo-resolve, the signature), instruments registering on a target (.reg, scroll-linked, see the registration group), a surface swept once then read (.mo-sweep), claims arriving in order of confidence (.mo-stagger), a measurement settling on a value (.mo-settle). The dither is already the brand's image language, so making it the motion language means the interface states the product's claim rather than describing it.
$extensions.pi.safety: Every hidden starting state is gated behind [data-js] and backed by a 2.5s reveal timeout. Animation is never load-bearing for legibility.

$extensions.pi.use: rail and pane width, toggle flip
landing-only atmosphere, CTA band grid reveal
Acquire, lock, release. Script writes a single --reg progress value (0 to 1 to 0) from the element's distance to the reading position; every mark is driven off it in CSS.
$extensions.pi.rationale: The corner brackets are the logo lockup's, so the brand signs its own interface. The arc — acquiring on entry, locking at the reading position, releasing on exit — is what makes it read as an instrument rather than an entrance animation.
$extensions.pi.constraint: REQUIRES SQUARED CORNERS. A right-angle bracket around a rounded box reads as a mistake, so the marks are suppressed under data-radius=soft rather than rendered badly. Also: one registered element per view. If two things are registered at once, neither is.
$extensions.pi.readout: Keep the tag to a few characters and make it say what was acquired. 'SOURCE 01 · INGESTED' is doing work; 'SCANNING…' is a film prop.

$extensions.pi.use: a single pass. Never loops; a loop is decoration.

registration.$description: Corner brackets that converge on an element as it reaches the reading position, lifted from the logo lockup so the brand signs its own interface.

$extensions.pi.ratio: One rule governs the mark: THE BRACKET IS AS THICK AS THE SPACE IT HOLDS OFF THE BOX. Stroke equals gap, both 6px, so the drawn weight and the clear space read as one measure rather than two. The arm is three quarters of a registered card's padding and the travel is arm plus gap. Never change one of the four on its own.
$extensions.pi.constraint: Requires squared corners. Suppressed under data-radius="soft" on purpose, because a right-angle bracket around a rounded box reads as a mistake.
$extensions.pi.restraint: One registered element per view. If two are registered at once, neither is. A registered card takes space.internal padding rather than the standard card padding, and at least space.clear below it, because the marks live outside the box.
$extensions.pi.history: 2026-09-24: an accent hairline drew across the top edge at lock. It was a third signal doing the job of the brackets and the readout, and at full width it read as a progress bar. Removed. The stroke was then 2px against a 6px gap, which read as a hairline sitting in a void; raising it to match the gap is what made the mark read as a drawn object.

$extensions.pi.use: bracket weight. Equals --reg-gap by rule; that equality is the whole design.
clear space between the bracket and the box edge. Three strokes.
length of each bracket arm. Three quarters of a registered card padding, so it aims into the corner without reaching the text.
how far outside the mark starts before converging. Arm plus gap. Drops to 10px under 640px, where the page gutter is narrower than the travel.
internal padding of a registered card, one step above the standard 24px. The brackets frame the corner from outside, so the corner inside has to be air.
minimum space below a registered element. At the usual section rhythm the brackets of one and the readout of the next collide.

$extensions.pi.drift: Three live values in the prototype: 104px in the shared block, 96px in rotary-a.html, 88px in beta.html, each introduced by re-declaring section{} after the block instead of editing it.

surface.$description: How a raised surface separates from the page. DEFAULT IS HAIRLINE as of 2026-09-24: no fill, no shadow, a pure drawn line. Components read all three tokens rather than assuming a fill exists. 'deep' and 'flat' were reviewed and dropped; 'warm' and 'wash' remain on the switch for comparison.

$extensions.pi.rationale: The border a fill needs, or the thing that does the separating alone when there is no fill.
The shadow a fill needs, or the thing that separates when there is neither fill nor border.

pi.options.hairline: DEFAULT. No fill and no shadow, a pure drawn line. Reads cleanest and frees the warm tone to mean something.
pi.options.warm: #F3EFE7 applied to every raised surface. Kept for comparison, but as a global treatment it spends the warm tone on ambience.
pi.options.wash: color-mix(--ink 4%, --bg) light / 5% dark. Neutral, tracks the theme, loses the temperature.

$extensions.pi.decision: 2026-09-24. Hairline and wash are used FREELY and alternate down a page to give it rhythm without temperature; hairline is the default. Warm is RATIONED to the extreme case where the extra chroma does something the other two cannot: one card in a group, a selected row, one band per page. Spreading warm globally, which is what the July decision did, spends the only tone that can mark importance on ambience.

$extensions.pi.rationale: The July warm tone, retained as a NAMED EMPHASIS SURFACE rather than the default. Applied with .warm on a component or .surface--warm on a band. This is what the tone became when hairline took over: it stopped being ambience and started meaning something.
$extensions.pi.constraint: Rare. Reserved for a selected or active row, the single most important card in a group, or one highlighted band per page. If two warm surfaces are visible at once, something is over-emphasised.

texture.$description: The dashed grid. A vignette applied to specific regions with .textured, never a page-wide wallpaper. It was under the entire page; texture that is everywhere is texture nowhere.

$extensions.pi.constraint: Anything sitting on a textured region must be OPAQUE. A translucent card shows dashes through its own face and reads as dirt rather than depth.

media.$description: Four tiers of image and motion, descending in loudness. At most one tier-1 element per page, and never two tiers competing in the same viewport.

$extensions.pi.constraint: All motion assets share one treatment: medium cell, 7% mono Bayer dither, greyscale, multiply blend (screen on dark surfaces). That treatment is the brand's image language; an undithered asset will look imported.
$extensions.pi.nonWhiteFootage: Footage shot against white composites onto the page with a multiply blend and the ground disappears. Footage that fills its frame has no white to blend away and stays a grey rectangle. Map its luminance through a seven-stop brand ramp instead, ordered BY LUMINANCE rather than by declaration index so one ramp is correct in both themes. Ship a single mono master and map it at runtime rather than baking colour per theme: the master is the smallest of the files and the only version that cannot go out of sync with the palette. Exploration, Pl. 14.

$extensions.pi.use: dithered loop behind the headline. One per page.
dithered loop behind a section. One per band.
a still diagram, chart or specimen. Framed and opaque.
